seo.metaTitle: Product Liability Help in South Lake Tahoe, CA
seo.metaDescription: Hurt by a defective product in South Lake Tahoe? Get a free case review from an attorney who handles California product liability claims. No fee unless you recover.

hero.subtitle: From faulty ski bindings on the slopes above Ski Run Boulevard to defective boat parts on the lake, defective products send South Lake Tahoe residents and visitors to the ER every season. We handle California product liability claims and can review your case at no cost.

about.title: South Lake Tahoe Product Liability Claims
about.longDescription: South Lake Tahoe's economy runs on recreation — ski resorts, marinas, rental shops along Lake Tahoe Boulevard and Pioneer Trail, and a steady stream of visitors renting gear they've never used before. That mix means defective products show up often: a snowboard binding that fails on a run, a rented paddleboard leash that snaps, a space heater that malfunctions in a rented cabin during winter. Under California law, injured people generally don't have to prove a manufacturer was careless — strict liability means showing the product itself was defective and that the defect caused the injury. Our team provides a free case review and can help you understand whether a manufacturer, distributor, or rental outfit may share responsibility. We'll help you preserve the product as evidence and explain your options. Our attorneys only get paid if you recover.

whyChoose.title: Why Talk to an Attorney About a Defective Product

items.title: You Don't Have to Prove Negligence
items.desc: California's strict liability rule means you generally only need to show the product was defective and caused your injury — not that anyone was careless in making it.

items.title: Multiple Parties Can Be Responsible
items.desc: Manufacturers, distributors, and retailers can all potentially be held liable, which matters in a tourist town where gear is often rented, resold, or shipped in from elsewhere.

items.title: The Product Itself Is Key Evidence
items.desc: We can advise you on preserving the defective item right away, since it's often the strongest proof of a design, manufacturing, or warning defect.

items.question: I was hurt using rental ski or snowboard gear in South Lake Tahoe — who's responsible?
items.answer: It depends on where the defect originated. If the equipment itself was poorly made or improperly maintained, the manufacturer, the rental shop, or both could potentially be liable. We can review the rental agreement and equipment history to sort out who may share responsibility.

items.question: Do I need to prove the manufacturer was negligent?
items.answer: No — California generally allows strict liability claims for defective products, meaning you typically just need to show the product was defective and that the defect caused your injury. This makes these cases different from many other personal injury claims.

items.question: What should I do with the product that hurt me?
items.answer: Keep it exactly as it was at the time of the injury, if it's safe to do so, and don't attempt repairs or alterations. Take photos, note where you got it, and avoid throwing it away — we can advise you on next steps for preserving it as evidence.

items.question: Is there a charge for a free case review?
items.answer: No. There is no cost to discuss your case, and we work on contingency, meaning we only get paid if you recover compensation. There's no cost or obligation to find out whether you have a claim.
